newsitem.title: CUBA: Elf, Cuba plan gas distribution venture.
newsitem.headline: Elf, Cuba plan gas distribution venture.

text.p: French oil firm Elf Aquitaine is discussing an agreement with the Cuban state under which cooking gas would be imported and distributed in cannisters to homes in eastern Cuba, company officials said Monday.

Pierre Moers, director for Africa, Overseas Territories and the Caribbean in Elf's refining and distribution division, and Cuba representative for company Guy Bruyere told reporters the venture would involve importing gas and bringing it to homes in four eastern provinces.

Production after five years of phasing in the gas supplies could reach 40,000 tonnes annually, they said. They gave no figures for the investment involved, but indicated the agreement could be signed in the coming months.
Elf currently has an agreement to mix lubricants at a plant in Santiago de Cuba in conjunction with a Cuban state-owned lubricants company.
The Elf company officials said production of this mix for machinery for the country's sugar industry was 150 tonnes last year. This year production is set to rise to 1,000 tonnes.
The Elf officials said they were not currently interested in refining oil in Cuba, or in exploration on the island.
